normalized_statement: forall n in Z, n>=0 => sum(k=1..n,2k-1)=n^2; empty_sum=0
proof: Induct on n. For n=0, both sides are 0. Assume sum_{k=1}^n(2k-1)=n^2. Then sum_{k=1}^{n+1}(2k-1)=n^2+(2(n+1)-1)=n^2+2n+1=(n+1)^2. Thus the result holds for every integer n>=0.
statement: For every integer n >= 0, with the empty sum defined as 0, sum_{k=1}^n (2k-1) = n^2.
title: Sum of the first n positive odd integers

normalized_statement: forall n in Z, n>=0 => sum(k=1..n,2k-1)=n^2; empty_sum=0
proof: The k-th odd number is approximately 2k. Therefore the sum is approximately n(n+1). Ignoring lower-order terms gives n^2, so the identity is exact.
